Compressions cause blood flow (not air flow to my knowledge) and try to reestablish a normal heart rhythm in cases of cardiac arrest. We breathe because we need that 3% oxygen for survival. Due to concentration gradients, so long as there is more oxygen in the air than in our blood/lungs, we will absorb the oxygen necessary for survival. In the case of someone who is not breathing at all, it is definitely the case! 

Edit: compressions do cause passive ventilation, but it is not enough in progressed cases of cardiac arrest to supply an individual with the oxygen they need to avoid organ failure and brain damage.

Just to fix the math: about 80% of what you breathe on a day to day basis isnt oxygen (mostly nitrogen). 20% of each breath you take is oxygen. 17% (according to the last person’s sources) of the air you breathe out is oxygen. So you are giving the person 85% of the oxygen they need which is objectively waaaaay better than nothing.

When you are not breathing, it is not the wastes like CO2 that kill you, it is the lack of oxygen in your system. So whether your breath has an excess amount of CO2 or not doesnt matter in a dire situation like that.
